about: Many smart TVs work out what's on their screen, this box's picture too, and send it to their maker for ads and recommendations. It's called ACR (automatic content recognition), and it's in the TV's own settings: Sofa Box can't switch it off for you. Pick your TV's brand to see where to look.
caveat: Menu names change between models and years, so yours may say it a little differently. The steps come from each maker's own help pages: the code on each brand opens them on your phone.

offline.title: Surest of all: keep the TV off the internet
offline.text: Sofa Box doesn't need the TV online. In the TV's network settings, forget your Wi-Fi, and leave its network socket empty: a TV that isn't online can't send what it sees. Its remote still works the box over HDMI.

brands.name: Samsung
steps: Press Home, go left to Menu, then Privacy Choices → Terms & Conditions, Privacy Policy.
Take back your agreement to Viewing Information Services (that's ACR) and to Interest-Based Advertisements, then OK.
An older set has the same choices in Settings, under Terms & Policy (Samsung's steps: Terms and Policy, then Interest Based Advertising).
brands.note: Samsung says ACR only runs if you agreed to Viewing Information Services, and that you can turn it off any time.

sources.title: Samsung: the Smart TV ACR feature
Samsung: privacy settings on your Smart TV

brands.name: LG
steps: Settings → All Settings → Support → Privacy & Terms → User Agreements.
Untick the Viewing Information agreement (ACR needs it) and the one for interest-based ads, and confirm.

Switch off Live Plus too, which works out what you're watching to show extras and ads: Settings → Advanced Settings → General → System → Additional Settings → Live Plus (webOS 21 to 23; older sets: All Settings → General → Additional Settings → Live Plus).
brands.note: LG says ACR is off until you accept the Viewing Information agreement, and stops when you take it back.

sources.title: LG: understanding privacy on LG smart TVs

brands.name: Vizio
steps: Menu → All Settings → Privacy & Legal → Viewing Data: Off. Older sets: Admin & Privacy → Viewing Data. VIA Plus sets: System → Reset & Admin → Viewing Data.
Menu → Privacy & Legal → Advertising → Limited Ad Tracking: On. Sets from before 2024: Admin & Privacy → Advertising; before 2020: System → Reset & Admin → Advertising.
Signed in with a Walmart account? Whether your VIZIO data is joined to Walmart's is a choice in your account at vizio.com/account, or in the VIZIO Mobile App.
brands.note: Vizio says it deletes the viewing data it logged when you turn Viewing Data off.

sources.title: Vizio: how to turn Viewing Data off

brands.name: Roku TV
brands.kind: TCL, Hisense and others with Roku built in
steps: Settings → Privacy → Smart TV experience: untick Use info from TV inputs (that's ACR).
Settings → Privacy → Advertising: switch off Personalize ads.
Settings → Privacy → Voice: untick Speech recognition (Roku uses your voice recordings to improve it).
brands.note: Roku stops from then on, but keeps what it collected before.

brands.name: Google TV
steps: Settings → Privacy → Ads → Delete advertising ID.
Then the TV maker's own setting: see Sony, TCL or Hisense here.
brands.note: Google says apps can still show ads, just not ones built on that ID.

sources.title: Google TV Help: change ad settings

brands.name: Sony
steps: Many BRAVIA sets have Samba TV, Sony's partner, recognising what's on screen: Settings → System Preferences → Samba Interactive TV (or Interactive TV Settings): Disable.
To have what it collected deleted, ask Samba TV: privacy@samba.tv.
Then, on a Google TV set, the Google TV steps here.
brands.note: Sony says disabling Samba Interactive TV stops it collecting what you watch.

sources.title: Sony: enable or disable Samba TV

brands.name: TCL
brands.kind: Roku TV and Google TV sets
steps: TCL makes Roku TV and Google TV sets: use the steps for the one yours has (its home screen shows which).
On its Google TV sets, TCL's own step is Settings → Privacy → Ads → Delete advertising ID.
brands.note: TCL's privacy policy says its advertising partners may use ACR and that you control it in the TV's settings, but not where.

brands.name: Hisense
brands.kind: Roku TV, Google TV, Fire TV and VIDAA sets
steps: Hisense makes Roku TV, Google TV, Fire TV and VIDAA sets: use the steps for the one yours has.
On its Google TV sets: Settings → System → Advanced System → Enhanced Viewing: switch off Automatic Content Recognition.
Its VIDAA sets aren't covered here yet.
brands.note: Hisense says Enhanced Viewing is only on if you chose it, and you can turn it off any time.

brands.name: Fire TV
brands.kind: Amazon Omni, Toshiba, Insignia and other sets with Fire TV built in
steps: Settings → Preferences → Privacy Settings: switch off Automatic Content Recognition, Device Usage Data, Collect App Usage Data and Interest-based Ads.
With an antenna plugged into the TV, the same menu has Amazon's setting for what you watch over the air: switch that off too.
Some sets also show these choices in your Amazon account: amazon.com/mycd → Privacy Settings → Amazon Devices Privacy.
brands.note: Amazon says turning ACR off doesn't change how the TV works, though ads may repeat more often.
